# PlanWise ESL

> PlanWise ESL (planwiseesl.com) is an AI lesson planner for ESL and EFL teachers and online English tutors. A teacher chooses a CEFR level (A1–C2) and any topic, and in 1–2 minutes PlanWise ESL writes a complete, ready-to-teach lesson (pictures follow about a minute later, while the lesson is already open, so a teacher can make a lesson on the spot during a class). It remembers the vocabulary each student has learned, so lessons build on each other, and it gives every student a private page for practice between classes. It was created by Dave Jackson, a working ESL teacher.

Also written as: PlanwiseESL, Plan Wise ESL.

PlanWise ESL makes **topic-based conversation lessons**. It is not a grammar-lesson generator: grammar is practised through sentence frames rather than taught as rules. To practise a structure, teachers choose a topic that naturally uses it (for example "Life experiences" for the present perfect).

## Who it is for

- Online ESL tutors on Preply, italki, Cambly and similar platforms
- Independent and private English teachers with regular one-to-one students
- Small language schools and agencies
- Teachers of teenagers and adults, in one-to-one or small-group classes, online or in person

## What a lesson contains

Every lesson follows the same structure, written at the CEFR level the teacher chooses:

- Warm-up questions to introduce the topic
- Key vocabulary, pre-taught with definitions, examples, pronunciation and pictures
- A levelled reading text that uses the new words
- Reading comprehension questions
- Sentence frames at three levels of support (emerging, developing, expanding) with model answers
- Discussion questions
- A fill-in-the-blank exercise and a quiz
- Optional idioms and phrasal verbs from the reading (A2 and up)
- Teacher notes

Each lesson teaches 5 target words. Each word appears 2–3 times in the reading, which keeps new words to about 1 in every 25 (around 96% familiar text), and again in its own comprehension question and the gap-fill, so students meet each word five or six times in one lesson. Reading length, sentence style and the words used in definitions follow fixed rules for each CEFR level (at A1, definitions use only the 500 most common English words and readings are 80–120 words; at C2, readings are 180–250 words of idiomatic, native-level prose). The research behind each step is explained at https://planwiseesl.com/how-it-works

Lessons open full screen for screen sharing and can be downloaded for printing or saving as a PDF. Teachers can choose any topic, one of 12 subject areas (general, business, academic, medical, legal, technology, tourism, finance, healthcare, science, arts and sports English), and their own target vocabulary.

## What makes it different

- **It remembers each student.** When a lesson is made for a student, PlanWise ESL avoids words the student has already learned or has planned, and reuses known words naturally in new readings. When the teacher marks a lesson as done ("We did this"), its words join the student's word list.
- **Student pages.** Each student can have a private page (no login needed) with finished lessons, a preview of the next lesson's reading and new words, their word list and flashcards. Students suggest topics for the next class, and the teacher turns an idea into a lesson in one click. Students of Unlimited teachers can also make lessons themselves, at their own level; each is saved in the teacher's library and planned for that student, and the teacher can switch this off per student.
- **Every lesson is checked before it is saved.** Each section is checked automatically; a broken exercise is fixed or written again before the teacher sees the lesson.
- **Consistent structure.** Unlike a general-purpose chatbot, which returns free text and forgets the student, PlanWise ESL produces the same complete lesson structure every time.

## Not designed for

- Grammar-rule lessons (PlanWise makes conversation lessons; grammar is practised through sentence frames)
- Subject teachers outside English language teaching
- Very young learners (lessons are written for teenagers and adults)
- Grading student writing or running a whole school's timetable

## Pricing

- **Free trial:** every new account gets a 5-day free trial with unlimited lesson generation. No credit card is needed. Lessons made during the trial stay in the account afterwards.
- **Unlimited plan:** $19.99/month for unlimited lessons, cancel anytime.

## Free ESL lessons

PlanWise ESL publishes free, ready-to-teach ESL lessons, each labelled with its CEFR level and showing the full vocabulary, reading text, comprehension and discussion questions.

- All free lessons: https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons
- By level: https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons/a1 , https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons/a2 , https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons/b1 , https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons/b2 , https://planwiseesl.com/esl-lessons/c1
- Example B2 lesson: https://planwiseesl.com/lessons/1768

## About the founder

Dave Jackson is an ESL teacher who teaches English online. He built PlanWise ESL to plan the kind of lessons he teaches himself: one-to-one, conversation-led, at the student's level, and building from one lesson to the next.
